Word quickly spread through the Burrows of Char'li and the mysterious stone and by the time the Festival of the Vine(A time of celebration held in honor of Zille and the invention of alcohol) had arrived and the changing of the Seasons Char'li had become quite the celebrity. However with fame comes envy and with envy comes hate.

Char'li, son of Dae'el and holder of the Coin of Tymoro paces nervously among the rows of mushrooms as he works with his den mates to assist preparations for the upcoming celebration. Word of the stone has reached Chief Ma'ten, leader of the tribe of Med'ja-Hom and he has requested that Char'li bring it before a meeting of elders so that they may examine and discuss the stone's power.

Char'li's reverie is broken by the sound of his den mates voice "Are you going to help with these mushrooms or are you going to just continue walk a hole in the floor?" "Sorry Sha'ne" Char'li's face burned with embarrassment as he bent to pick up one of the large mushrooms grown by the Med'ja. Growing to knee height and with radius about twice as wide as an adult Med'ja the Mushrooms are an important part of the Med'jan diet supplying them with much of the energy necessary to expand their homes and fuel the hunt.

"You've been distracted a lot lately" Sha'ne groaned, adjusting her grip on the oversized mushroom "I can't help it" groaned Char'li in reply, taking hold of the mushroom's other side. "It's the stone, I can't stop thinking about it" "What is it that bothers you about it?" "Ever since I found the stone things have been different" "Different how?" "it's hard to explain but It feels as though the Gods have given me both a blessing and a curse" The two lowered the Mushroom Sha'ne nodding her head in encouragement.

"I survived the tunnel collapse without and I've been given audience with the Elders, these things are good yet at the same time I feel an evil wind blowing through the tunnels of the Burrows, glances, whispers of ill intent. Several times I found that the stone had vanished without cause, though I suspect it was stolen, only for it to reappear shortly after."

The two were now sitting beside the Mushroom, Sha'ne looking upon Char'li with concern. "If the stone bothers you so why do you not rid yourself of it? Bury it in secret or cast it into the deepest pool you can find?" "That its what concerns me most." Char'li replied, his voice hollow "No matter how I try to rid myself of the accursed stone be it pond or burial it returns to me unbidden and unannounced"

Sha'ne stood and brushed the dirt from her fur "Then it is good that you will be meeting with the Elders soon. For now you must set aside your worries over the stone and leave it to the Gods, there is much work to do before the celebration."

- - -

Save for the sound of crackling fire the Cave of the Elders was Silent. Char'li son of Dae'el stood before the Council of Elders, the heat of the fire licking at his back. Roused from his slumber during the darkest part of night and escorted via guard the Elders had taken Char'li by surprise leaving him shaken and afraid.

The Elders were seated at the back of the cave in a half circle. Chief Ma'Ten sat at the centre of the group gazing impassibly at the young Med'ja standing before him, to his right sat his brother Se'Kin the blind representative of the Cult of Umbralocht, the fire-light mirrored in his milky-white eyes giving him an other-worldly appearance. To the left sat Me'de the great Den Mother while bordering the group were Lo'te and Ma'te, twin siblings who held share the role of Master and Mistress of the Hunt and War Chief.

Chief Ma'Ten broke the silence of the room, his voice rumbling deep like thunder speaking slowly and deliberately. "Members of the council, Before we gathered you each of you had heard rumor of the stone blessed by the gods and of the child who wields it. Now that you have heard his story and he has presented the stone before the council what say you?

Sek'in spoke second, his voice tired and worn from his years of research and consumption "It is clear that the stone contains some magical enchantment, however due to the nature of the stone's attachment to the boy, in-depth study may prove difficult. My recommendation is for the boy to be sent to the surface to live among my brothers and I so that we may examine the stone together and learn it's secrets".

The Shaman's words sent a chill throughout the young Med'ja's body and he began to feel very cold, to leave the safety of the Burrows at his age was tantamount to suicide. He had never handled a weapon nor been instructed in proper plantlore for foraging. On the surface, even under the guardianship of the Cult of Umbralocht Char'li would be at the mercy of the gods.

Me'le was the next to speak, her words as though she had read the young mans mind "Sending the Child to live among the Shamans is a ludicrous idea, it would be kinder to kill him here and now. While it is true the stone displays some magic properties thus far it has done little harm aside from serving as a cause of vexation to some would be thieves. Therefore my recommendation is that the child be left to grow amongst his kin until such times the child comes of age whereby he can make his own decision or until the gods reveal their purpose and the council reconvened.

The twins Lo'te and Ma'te spoke as one, giving their words a magical, music like quality. "While we agree sending the child to the surface would be condemning him to death we do not agree that the child should be left to grow unchecked. Our recommendation is that the child and the stone be sequestered within the confines of the Burrow but separated from the tribe until the power of the stone reveals itself.

A treasure to be unlocked, a child to be protected, a danger to ward against. The Elder's words spoke of all these things yet only the word of Ma'Ten was law. The Chieftain considered their words carefully, the wellbeing and continuation of the tribe was paramount yet each life was a gift from the Gods themselves, a promise for the future. He observed the child who had stood before them unmoving during the entire ordeal, though still young his body was strong, a reward for his dedication to the tribe and it was clear from the questioning that his mind was unaffected by illness nor malice. Should this not be proof enough of the stone's benign nature?

The Chieftain rose, stepping into the centre of the room "Council Members I have listened to your words and while it is true we do not yet understand the true nature of the stone the child possesses I would be remiss if I allowed us to repeat the mistakes of the past, Therefore I decree that the child shall grow amongst his kin as Hom intended. Should the power of the stone become a danger to the child or to those around him he shall be turned over to the Hunter Masters until he is of age, this is the law so sayeth Chief Ma'Ten, 9th Chieftain of the tribe of Med'ja-Hom and Master of the Southern Lands.

Upon his return to the den Char'li slept late into the following day, awaking to echoes of celebration with the commons of the Burrows and the bitter scent of alchohol in the air warning him that he was not alone. "Hello?" he called out into the darkness, sounds of movement coming from a door to the left "So, you're awake" the voice replied with a slur. More sounds of movement. "The Council's golden child" A figure lurched into the room hunched over and using a spear for balance.

"I'm sorry?" the young Med'jan replied, rising from his bed apprehensively. "We've all heard the stories" the voice slurred back "About the boy who found a stone that protects him from harm, the boy The Elders called to meet before he was even of age" Char'li backed away as the figure shuffled forward and he could now see that it was Dae'lon, a young warrior who had become of age prior to the last celebration. "A gift such as that is wasted on a child like you, in the hands of a warrior like me the holder would become strong beyond compare, rivalling even that of the Chieftain himself!"

"Dae'lon please" Char'li pleaded "The alchohol has affected your mind and filled your heart with darkness, I would gladly give you the stone myself were it possible but the gods have bound it to me" "THEN WE SHALL UNBIND YOU!" Dae'lon roared, throwing himself upon the child with a leap.

Together they struggled rolling back and forth across the den overturning bedding and belongings alike, the stronger and inebriated Dae'lon against the younger and quick witted Char'li. Try as he might the young Med'ja could not surmount his older comrade and was quickly overpowered, long sinewy fingers clasping around his supple young neck like a vice.

Char'li's vision began to darken as Dae'lon's grip grew ever tighter, squeezing, searching, begging for the crack of bone and popping of flesh. Char'li's hands scrabbled across the den floor as he searched, hoping beyond hope that something, anything would meet his grasp and free him from his assailant. Just as he had given up home the young Med'jan's fingers brushed against something small and smooth, he brought it up, striking it against the side of the drunken Med'jan's head with all his might and was rewarded with the sound of a metalic "Clink!" mixed with a loud "Crack!" as Dae'lon collapsed beside him.

Char'li gasped for air, coughing and hacking as his vision slowly returned and he realised that this time, without a doubt, his life had been saved by the stone.

Dae'lon lay deathly still, his chest rising and falling as he drew sharp, ragged breaths, a crimson trail of blood running down the side of his face and pooling on the floor.

With the now Bloodstained coin in hand Char'li fled the den running deeper and deeper into the Burrows, far from Dae'lon and far from the celebrations of the Festival of the Vine. Light gave way to darkness and eventually Char'li found that he was completely, inextricably lost and so, his energy spent, the young Med'ja collapsed and began to cry.

Sometime after his tears had dried and the darkness of despair had been replaced by the void of sleep Char'li woke once again to the scratching sound of shuffling footsteps. The grip of fear clutching his chest the young Med'ja pressed himself against the wall of the tunnel the stone gripped tight in his hand. "Fear not my child" a voice called out, tired and worn "I have not come to bring you death nor have I come to hand you over to subjugation. What I bring is merely opportunity and a chance at destiny"

Char'li, son of Dae'el, bearer of the coin of Tymoro stepped away from the tunnel wall and into the light of the Elder's torch. Though his eyes were covered with a milky-white cloud brought on from his consumption of blindweed Char'li got the distinct impression that the Elder could see more than just the tunnel and figure before him.

Extending a small waterskin the Elder spoke, his voice little more than a whisper "Take this child and drink from it" "What will it do?" the child asked, extending his hand with hesitation "The effects are...unpredictable" the Elder answered with a smile, deepening the lines on his scarred, pock marked face "My hope is that it shall allow you to commune with the Gods to unlock the secrets of that stone and change your fate"

"My fate?" The boy replied, taking the waterskin from the Elder's hand. "Yes, I fear tonight's events may have set into motion a chain of events that cannot be undone. Not only may you lose your life but the secrets of the stone could be lost forever." Char'li nodded sadly as he remembered the struggle with Dae'lon and the ragged breathes he made as he lay upon the den floor. Char'li regarded the open water skin with suspicion "And you do not know what this will do?" The Shaman shook his head sadly "I am sorry child but it is in the hands of the gods"

Char'li drained the contents of the waterskin in a single motion, the acrid, bitter contents stinging his throat as it passed through to his stomach. Dropping to his knees as his stomach began to harden and his body began to tremble the Elder's words echoed in his mind. "I am sorry child but it is in the hands of the gods....."
